content.en: The **International Labour Organization (ILO)** is the only tripartite UN agency, bringing together representatives of governments, employers, and workers. Its primary objective is to advance social and economic justice by setting **international labor standards**. These standards are formulated through **Conventions** and **Recommendations**, which serve as blueprints for national labor legislation.

content.en: India is a founding member of the ILO and has ratified several core conventions, influencing the recent consolidation of labor laws into four major codes.

content.en: Students often confuse ILO conventions with mandatory global laws; they are only binding once a member state formally ratifies them.
